text:
Connor McDavid's point streak is over, and Daily Faceoff Edmonton mourned it accordingly. It ran long enough to draw Wayne Gretzky in: Sportskeeda carried his line, "Hope he breaks all my records." Meanwhile the Toronto Sun wrote about McDavid buying a new Toronto home "fuelling fresh Maple Leafs speculation." That is the kind of attention 57 points in 25 games brings.

The numbers are absurd: 44 assists, 27 power-play points, 23.6 minutes a night, a scoring rate of 5.8 points per 60 against a talent range from us of 4.07 to 4.95. His top skating speed sits in the 100th percentile, and Evolving-Hockey had him first among 401 forwards in wins above replacement last season.

Some of it will come back to earth. Edmonton has scored 25.7 more goals than its chances deserved with him on, one of the largest gaps we track, and over his last ten games the chances with him on dipped below his norm. Mike Babcock splitting him from Leon Draisaitl is the change to watch. Our range for his season: 146 to 179 points.
